items.issues: 'He did not seem torn, only careful to honor each' states the answer almost directly; A is a clean plot-summary distractor, but overall closer to easy than medium.
Requires combining 'stopped calling on me' + 'silence was never indifference, only waiting'; B is a good anecdote-summary distractor. Solid medium.
Trigger (girl's question) + 'still tuned his strings to Dewi's flute' must be linked; C is a tempting outcome-as-motive misread but unsupported. Fine.
Shaking hands + 'recipes on paper got lost' + repeated lessons must be chained; D borrows passage words but is not stated. Good.
B is the intended result-as-motive misread ('sewed until the lamps were lit'); C is weak/odd. D slightly longest but not formally revealing.
Weighting task works: A/B overweight the uncertainty, D is wrong register. Clean.
B is the near-miss (regret overweighted); most of the passage is fond memory with the letter as a single 'Yet'. D holds, but B will attract a share of test-takers as intended.
C flips the weighting (narrator keeps coat buttoned, sets mug down undrunk); B overstates forgiveness. Good proportion question.
Softer repetition of 'sorry' + sliding the envelope must be joined; C misassigns the apology. Fine.
A and B each reflect one side only; D contradicted by taking his arm. Works.
Repeated 'pretended not to notice / pretended the same' makes A fairly direct; B contradicted (Aydin knows), C reverses debt direction. Closer to easy.
Priest's line 'tied with that same line, and it never seems to break' plus folding the ticket points plainly to B; C is the only mildly tempting distractor.
'You'll have your own floors soon' + daughter finishing the sweep makes C clear; B is a partial reading, A/D weak.
'a field no one had walked across yet' and 'whatever he decided to put there' nearly paraphrase D; A is a reasonable foil via 'worse things than films'.
Option D names 'Freja' but the narrator is never named in the passage — fix option text (e.g., 'the narrator'). Otherwise sound; B is a good foil from the nurses' teasing.
Options assert 'brothers' though the passage never gives the siblings' gender (Hala is usually a female name) — use 'siblings'. C is a nice literal-minded foil contradicted by the cost line.
Preceding sentence ('polite way of telling her to stop sitting in the dark') makes C direct; D is the literal-anger foil. Easy.
'high enough that no one would come to thank him' is in the same sentence as the figure; D is nearly a restatement. Easy.
